analysis.title: Flight-to-quality helps belly richen
key_insights: After flight-to-quality trades at the start of the week, markets focus on October retail sales data (17 Nov) and FOMC minutes (18 Nov).

CACIB economists forecast October retail sales headline at 0.0% MoM versus 0.8% MoM in September, with consumers spending despite the surge in gas prices from the Iran war. That would leave ex-auto and gas at 0.3% MoM.
The FOMC minutes are expected to show the rationale for the October skip. Market participants want to know why the Fed did not hike in October.

Before the upside surprise in the October CPI data last week, Fed Governor Chris Waller put a 50bp hike on the table for December. Dallas Fed president Lorie Logan also speculated on accelerating the pace of hikes.
The market prices about 27bp of hikes by December and 44bp by January.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh spoke about AI's potential impact on the economy rather than monetary policy, consistent with his practice of not giving forward guidance. He cited AI risks from bad actors and the Fed's review of potential vulnerabilities.
CACIB is biased towards curve flatteners because additional rate hikes would weigh on short rates.
The intermediate sector has been highly volatile. It cheapened in last week's Treasury selloff, then the 2-5-10Y butterfly richened about 3bp in yesterday's flight-to-quality rally.
